## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

132	### 4.2 PEP 440 局部版本陷阱：裸 pip install 为什么会静默换 torch
133	
134	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
135	
136	三条 PEP 440 规则合谋出一个陷阱：
137	
138	1. **局部版本参与排序**：\( v < v{+}\ell \)（同公开版本下带标签的高于不带的），标签之间**逐段**比较（数值段按数、字母段按字典序）。
139	2. **不带标签的 specifier 忽略候选的标签**：`==0.2.0` 匹配 `0.2.0` 和所有 `0.2.0+…`。
140	3. **pip 在多个匹配中取最高版本**。
141	
142	于是对任何容纳了多于一行 wheel 的文件集（`--find-links`、`--extra-index-url`、一个装满 wheel 的目录、乃至 PyPI 本身），不带标签的请求都解析到**排序最高的那个标签**——与本机 torch 是什么完全无关。
143	
144	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
145	
146	一次 release 的 9 个版本工件（8 带标签 + 1 无标签）的排序链：
147	
148	\[ \texttt{0.2.0} < \texttt{0.2.0+torch210cu128} < \texttt{0.2.0+torch210cu130} < \texttt{0.2.0+torch211cu128} < \cdots < \texttt{0.2.0+torch213cu130} \]
149	
150	specifier 语义形式化：
151	
152	\[ v \in \mathrm{match}(\texttt{==0.2.0}) \iff v_{\text{public}} = \texttt{0.2.0} \quad (\text{标签被忽略}) \]
153	
154	由此，「裸 `pip install fast-ulysses`」的完整事故链是：
155	
156	```text
157	pip install fast-ulysses
158	  └─ PyPI 只有 torch213cu130（无标签形式），无需选择
159	     └─ 其元数据 Requires-Dist: torch==2.13.*
160	        └─ 本机 torch 2.11 不满足 → pip 不会失败，
161	           而是从 PyPI 装 torch 2.13（不同的 torch、不同的 CUDA 构建）
162	              └─ 报告为「普通的依赖解析」→ 无任何警告
163	```
164	
165	两条续发症：装完后再把 torch 重装回 2.11，就得到 4.4 的 `undefined symbol`；而之后任何 `pip install fast-ulysses` 都打印 `Requirement already satisfied`，**错误的行原地不动**（`--upgrade` 也只会升到最高标签）。唯一的根治是把标签写全：`fast-ulysses==0.2.0+torch210cu128`。
166

233	### 4.3 wheel-url 匹配顺序：machine → python → torch minor → CUDA major
234	
235	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
236	
237	`wheel-url` 回答「当前环境该装哪个 wheel」。四根轴的**检查顺序不是随意的**：`_match` 的 docstring 说得很清楚——按「各轴被谁决定」排序：machine 与 python 是 **wheel 自身的 tag**（auditwheel/setuptools 决定，装完就不可变），先查；torch minor 与 CUDA major 是 **`.so` 钉住的轴**，需要现场读 torch 才能查。
238	
239	两个容易忽略的精度选择：
240	
241	- **CUDA 只比 major**：扩展从 toolkit 只链 `libcudart.so.<major>`，check_wheel.py 断言的也恰是这么多——所以 `12.8` 与 `12.9` 的环境装同一个 `cu128`/`cu129` 行（按各自 major）。
242	- **torch minor 按整数比较**：`_abi` 把 `"2.9"` 转成 `(2, 9)`、`"2.10"` 转成 `(2, 10)`。字符串排序会给出 `"2.9" > "2.10"` 的假象——这与 PEP 440 对公开版本的数值语义是同一个陷阱。
243	
244	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
245	
246	`_match` 的完整判定序（伪代码）：
247	
248	```text
249	_match(matrix, live, machine):
250	  1 machine  ≠ matrix.machine      → "no wheel for {machine}…"           + 源码构建
251	  2 python   ∉ matrix.pythons      → "no wheel for {python}…"            + 换解释器/源码构建
252	  3 torch 不可导入（"unimportable"）→ "torch does not import here…"       + 先装 torch
253	  4 torch_abi ∉ 发布的 minor 集合   → "no wheel for torch {abi}…"
254	        │  附「.so 嵌 c10d::Work 虚表/pybind11/TORCH_LIBRARY」的解释
255	        └ 选项：pip install "torch=={最近的发布 minor}.*" 再跑一次，或源码构建
256	  5 same = 同 minor 的行; majors = 它们的 CUDA major 集合
257	    live.cuda ∈ {None, unknown}    → CPU/ROCm torch，每个 wheel 都链 libcudart
258	    live.cuda.major ∉ majors       → "no wheel for CUDA {cuda}…
259	                                      A CUDA major mismatch fails at import on
260	                                      libcudart, and no LD_LIBRARY_PATH fixes it."
261	  6 返回 same 中 CUDA major 相同的那一行（next(...)）
262	```
263	
264	第 4 步的「最近建议」逻辑：live 的 minor 低于最低发布值时建议最低那档，否则（高于最高档）建议最高那档。

319	       ({**base, "torch": "2.12.5+cu129", "torch_abi": "2.12", "cuda": "12.9"}, "x86_64"),  # 命中
320	   ]:
321	       r = cli._match(matrix, live, machine)
322	       print("->", r if isinstance(r, str) else f"ROW {r}")
323	   ```
324	
325	**需要观察的现象**：四组输入各自的返回；注意第 2 组先过 machine 关、再倒在 torch minor 关，输出并不提 python。
326	
327	**预期结果**（由 `_match` 的分支决定）：
328	
329	- aarch64 → `no wheel for aarch64: every published wheel is manylinux_2_28_x86_64.` + 源码构建选项；
330	- torch 2.9 → `no wheel for torch 2.9: published for torch 2.10, 2.11, 2.12, 2.13.` + ABI 论证 + `pip install "torch==2.10.*"`（低于最低发布档，near 取最低）；

336	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
337	
338	**练习 1**：为什么 machine 检查在 python 之前、python 检查在 torch 之前？
339	**答案**：按「被谁决定」排序（docstring L132-134）。machine/python 是 wheel 文件名自带的 tag，与现场 torch 无关，不读 torch 就能排除；torch minor 与 CUDA major 要 `import torch` 现场读取——包括「torch 根本导不了」这种情况本身也是先检后查（L150）。
340	
341	**练习 2**：torch 2.14（假设高于全部发布行）的环境跑 `wheel-url`，`near` 建议是哪个？为什么不是「最近的」2.13 之外的东西？
342	**答案**：`near = abis[-1]` 即 2.13——`_abi(live) > _abi(abis[-1])` 时取最高发布档（L158）。建议的语义是「降到已发布的最近一档」，因为高于矩阵的 torch 只能装源码构建（sdist 对着已装 torch 编译），消息末尾的 `_FROM_SOURCE` 就是那条路。
343	
344	**练习 3**：`wheel-url` 为什么打印 `--find-links <expanded_assets>` 而不是一个直接指向 `.whl` 的 URL？
345	**答案**：见 cli.py L224-231 的注释——文件名里的平台 tag 由 auditwheel 压缩决定（出现过双 tag），写死文件名是猜；release 页面 HTML 不含 `.whl` 链接、对 pip 无用；`expanded_assets` 是页面懒加载资产列表的片段，列出全部 36 个文件，让 pip 自己按 tag 挑。
346	
347	### 4.4 导入失败归因：_diagnose 的四分类
348	
349	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
350	
351	`.so` 加载失败时，`ld.so` 只会说两种话：`undefined symbol: _ZN3c10…`（某个 mangled 符号找不到）或 `libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file`（某个 soname 找不到）。**两种话都不说本项目的两根钉子轴——torch minor、CUDA major——哪根错了**。`_diagnose` 的职责就是补上这个命名：拿两份数据做对照——
352	
353	- **built 侧**：`_build_meta.py` 里 setup.py 烘进去的构建事实（`TORCH_ABI`、`CUDA_VERSION` 等）；
354	- **live 侧**：当前环境的 `torch.__version__`、`torch.version.cuda`、解释器 tag。
355	
356	它只在失败路径上被导入（「working load pays nothing for it」）。
357	
358	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
359	
360	`_verdict` 的分支表（按代码顺序）：
361	
362	| # | 条件 | 归因 | 修复指向 |
363	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
364	| 1 | live torch 本身导不了 | 「loader 报错是 torch 自己的」 | 先修/装 torch |
365	| 2 | built 为空（`_build_meta.py` 缺失） | 「unknown build，无从对照」 | 重新构建或换正规 wheel |
366	| 3 | 报错含 `undefined symbol` 且 minor 失配 | **torch minor ABI 不匹配** | 装与本 torch 配套的构建 |
367	| 4 | 报错含 `undefined symbol` 且 minor 一致 | 「缺的符号不是 torch minor 引起的」 | 另找原因 |
368	| 5 | 报错含 `libcudart` 且 major 失配 | **CUDA major 不匹配** | 装对应 CUDA major 的行 |
369	| 6 | 报错含 `libcudart` 且 major 一致 | 「cudart 装了但没有地方找得到它」 | 查 torch/nvidia wheel 安装 |
370	| 7 | 以上皆不中 | 「loader 消息本身就是全部」 | 兜底 |
371	
372	一个容易忽略的细节：`explain` 报告的**主语**是动态选择的——torch 导不了时报 `torch failed to load`，否则报 `fast_ulysses._C failed to load`。因为 `__init__.py` 里 `import torch` 先于 `import ._C`，把 torch 的失败错怪到 `_C` 头上会把读者引向错误的排查方向。
373	
374	归因的**前提是 built 侧事实为真**——这正是发布管线里 check_wheel.py 的工作（4.4.3 末条）。
375	
376	#### 4.4.3 源码精读
377	
378	失败入口与包装：
379	
380	[python/fast_ulysses/__init__.py:L3-L10](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/__init__.py#L3-L10) —— 先 `import torch`（在 `_C` dlopen 前把 libtorch 装载好），再 `from . import _C`；任何 ImportError 都先经 `_diagnose.explain` 包装成带归因的消息再 `raise … from exc`。所以 `fast-ulysses doctor` 在扩展坏掉时同样抛这份报告而不是运行（cli.py L26-29 的 `_load` docstring 交代了这条路径的分工）。
381	
382	built 侧与 live 侧的采集：
383	
384	[python/fast_ulysses/_diagnose.py:L13-L26](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/_diagnose.py#L13-L26) —— `build_meta()` 先试相对导入再试平名（cli.py 以文件运行时没有包可相对），两败俱空返回 `{}`——对应分支 2。
385	
386	[python/fast_ulysses/_diagnose.py:L29-L41](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/_diagnose.py#L29-L41) —— `_live()` 导不了 torch 时记 `"unimportable"`/`"unknown"`（torch 导不了本身就是一个候选原因），并给出 `torch_abi`（前两段）与 `cp` tag。
387	
388	归因主体：
389	
390	[python/fast_ulysses/_diagnose.py:L44-L70](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/_diagnose.py#L44-L70) —— 分支表 1-7 的实现：`undefined symbol` 比对 `TORCH_ABI`（L52-62），`libcudart` 比对 CUDA **major**（L63-69，与 `_match` 的精度选择一致）。
391	
392	[python/fast_ulysses/_diagnose.py:L73-L85](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/_diagnose.py#L73-L85) —— `explain` 的输出格式：主语（torch 还是 `_C`）+ 归因句 + `built against:`（烘进去的全部事实）+ `installed now:` + `loader error:`（loader 的原话永远在末尾）。
393	
394	built 侧事实的产地：
395	
396	[setup.py:L149-L171](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/setup.py#L149-L171) —— `_write_build_meta` 在扩展旁写出 `VERSION/WHEEL_TAG/TORCH_VERSION/TORCH_ABI/CUDA_VERSION/PYTHON_ABI/CUDA_ARCH_LIST/HAS_WORK_REGISTRY`。docstring 点明时机：`build_info()` 在 dlopen 本身失败时无法应答，而这正是需要这些事实的时刻。
397	
398	发布前的「事实为真」保证（归因能成立的前提）：
399	
400	[tools/check_wheel.py:L185-L219](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/tools/check_wheel.py#L185-L219) —— 断言 wheel 的 `Requires-Dist` 确有 `torch=={TORCH_ABI}.*`，且 `_build_meta` 的 CUDA major 与构建容器一致（「cu13 的 torch 在 CUDA 12 镜像里构建会链 libcudart.so.12、然后在 cu13 运行时上死」——下游没有任何东西能发现）。
401	
402	[tools/check_wheel.py:L222-L252](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/tools/check_wheel.py#L222-L252) —— `_check_wheel_tag` 把文件名里的 local version **反解**回 torch/CUDA 版本，与 `_build_meta` 对照：release.yml 的 `tag:` 是自由文本，若标签写 `torch212cu130` 而实际 torch 是 2.11，其余断言全过、发出去的文件名在撒谎。
403	
404	用户面的特征对照：
405	
406	[docs/install.md:L187-L207](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md#L187-L207) —— 两种典型报错的语义：`undefined symbol: _ZN3c10…` = wheel 的 torch minor 与已装 torch 不符（含「pip 把 torch 搬走后又装回来」的续发症）；`libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file` = CUDA-12 wheel 在 CUDA-13 环境（或反之），`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 修不了。修复顺序：先查 torch 是不是你选的那个，再 uninstall + 重装。
407	
408	#### 4.4.4 代码实践
409	
410	**实践目标**：亲手触发一次导入失败并读懂归因；再用伪造的 built/live 直接调 `_verdict`，拿到 torch-minor 与 CUDA-major 两类消息的原文。
411	
412	**操作步骤**：
413	
414	1. 在**未构建**的源码树（没有 `_C`、没有 `_build_meta.py`；torch 可导入）上触发失败：
415	
416	   ```bash
417	   PYTHONPATH=python python -c "import fast_ulysses"
418	   ```
419	
420	2. 平名导入 `_diagnose`（纯 stdlib），伪造两侧数据（示例代码）：
421	
422	   ```python
423	   # drive_verdict.py —— 复现两类归因消息
424	   import sys
425	   sys.path.insert(0, "python/fast_ulysses")
426	   import _diagnose  # noqa: E402
427	
428	   built = {"TORCH_ABI": "2.12", "CUDA_VERSION": "12.9"}
429	   live = {"torch": "2.13.0+cu130", "torch_abi": "2.13", "cuda": "13.0", "python": "cp312"}
430	   print(_diagnose._verdict("undefined symbol: _ZN3c10I…", built, live), end="\n---\n")
431	   print(_diagnose._verdict("libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file", built, live))
432	   ```
433	
434	**需要观察的现象**：第 1 步的报错不再是裸 ModuleNotFoundError，而是四行结构的报告；第 2 步两条消息分别命中分支 3 与分支 5。
435	
436	**预期结果**：
437	
438	- 第 1 步（未构建树 + torch 可导入）：
439	
440	  ```text
441	  fast_ulysses._C failed to load: unknown build: _build_meta.py is missing, so there is nothing to compare against.
442	    built against: unknown build
443	    installed now: torch=<本机版本>, cuda=<本机 CUDA>, python=cp<XX>
444	    loader error: No module named 'fast_ulysses._C'
445	  ```
446	
447	- 第 2 步第一条（分支 3）：`built against torch 2.12, but torch 2.13 is installed, and a torch minor bump changes the C++ ABI this extension links against. Install a build made for this torch.`
448	- 第二条（分支 5）：`built for CUDA 12.9, but torch reports CUDA 13.0. Install the build whose CUDA major matches this torch.`
449	
450	第 1 步的 `installed now:` 一行内容随环境而变，报告骨架与第一行是确定的——**待本地验证**。
451	
452	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
453	
454	**练习 1**：装了 `torch210cu128` 行的 wheel，然后单独把 torch 升到 2.13。`import fast_ulysses` 的归因是哪一类？为什么不是 CUDA 类？
455	**答案**：分支 3——报错含 `undefined symbol`（torch 2.13 里旧 mangled 名字没了），且 `built["TORCH_ABI"]="2.10" ≠ live["torch_abi"]="2.13"`。CUDA 类（分支 5/6）只在报错提到 `libcudart` 时进入；torch 升级不动 soname 的 major，`libcudart` 还找得到。
456	
457	**练习 2**：为什么 `_verdict` 里 CUDA 比较用 `split(".")[0]`（只比 major），而 torch 比较用完整 minor？
458	**答案**：两根轴的钉法不同。扩展从 toolkit 只链 `libcudart.so.<major>`（check_wheel 的 REQUIRED_NEEDED 断言），所以 CUDA minor 无关；而 torch 的 C++ ABI 在 minor 边界上变化（vtable、pybind11、TORCH_LIBRARY 注册），minor 必须精确。`_match`（L136-137）与 `_requires()`（setup.py）做的是同一组精度选择——三处必须一致，否则会出现「wheel-url 挑的行与实际能运行的行不同」。
459	
460	**练习 3**：分支 6（`libcudart` 在报错里、CUDA major 却一致）是什么事故？
461	**答案**：cudart 本身装了、major 也对，但没有任何搜索路径找得到它——典型的是 torch/nvidia 的 pip wheel 安装残缺或环境被破坏。这已经**不是**矩阵选行问题，`_verdict` 如实说「cudart is installed where nothing finds it」，把排查引向安装面而非发布面。
462	
463	## 5. 综合实践
464	
465	把本讲四条线串成一次「发布面巡检 + 事故演练」：
466	
467	**任务 A：矩阵巡检脚本**。写一个 `audit_matrix.py`（示例代码，读者完成）：
468	
469	1. 读 `wheel_matrix.json`，对 8 行各伪造一个命中的 `live`（如 torch `2.11.3+cu130`、cuda `13.0`、python `cp311`、machine `x86_64`），断言 `_match` 恰好返回该行；
470	2. 对四根轴各伪造一个失配（aarch64 / cp39 / torch 2.9 / CUDA 11.8），断言返回的字符串**第一行**分别以 `no wheel for aarch64`、`no wheel for cp39`、`no wheel for torch 2.9`、`no wheel for CUDA 11.8` 开头；
471	3. 断言 PyPI 行恰为最后一行，且 `_tag(该行)` 是对全部行做 `max(..., key=标签的 PEP 440 排序)` 的胜者——用 4.2 的 `packaging` 手法验证。
472	
473	**任务 B：三份事故报告**。每份不超过 10 行，写清「现场报错原文（首行）→ `_diagnose` 归因分支 → 修复命令」：
474	
475	1. 裸 `pip install fast-ulysses` 后 torch 被搬到 2.13（用 `python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda)"` 取证）；
476	2. 装了错误行（torch210cu128）后又重装了 torch 2.11——预期 `undefined symbol`，归因分支 3；
477	3. CUDA-12 行的 wheel 装在 CUDA-13 的 torch 环境里——预期 `libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file`，归因分支 5，修复必须含 `pip uninstall -y fast-ulysses`。
478	
479	判据：报告里的归因句应与 `_diagnose._verdict` 的输出逐字一致（用 4.4.4 的驱动脚本核对），修复命令应与 `wheel-url` 打印的形式一致（写全标签或走索引）。多 GPU 不是本实践的前提；若无可导入的 torch，任务 A 仍可完整运行（它不碰 torch），任务 B 以纸面推演完成并标注「待本地验证」。
480	
481	## 6. 本讲小结
482	
483	- 一次 release 是 **36 个 wheel**：8 个 (torch minor × CUDA major) 行 × 4 个 CPython，加 4 个去掉 local version 上 PyPI 的无标签行；`wheel_matrix.json` 是这张矩阵的机器可读快照，`test_wheel_matrix.py` 是它与 release.yml 之间唯一的同步检查。
484	- PEP 440 的三条规则（局部版本参与排序、无标签的 specifier 忽略标签、pip 取最高）合谋出**静默换 torch**：任何多行文件集上，裸 `pip install fast-ulysses` 都解析到 `+torch213cu130`，再用其 `torch==2.13.*` pin 把你的 torch 搬走——唯一的根治是把标签写全，或走不含 torch 的专用索引让 pip 回溯。
485	- `wheel-url` 的 `_match` 按「被谁决定」排序四根轴：machine/python（wheel 自身 tag）在前，torch minor/CUDA major（`.so` 钉住的轴）在后；CUDA 只比 major，因为扩展从 toolkit 只链 `libcudart.so.<major>`；每个失败分支都给出可执行选项并统一收尾在源码构建命令上。
486	- 导入失败时 `ld.so` 的两种话（`undefined symbol` / 缺 `libcudart` soname）都不指认哪根轴；`_diagnose` 用「`_build_meta` 的构建事实 vs `_live` 的现场」对照完成归因，且报告主语动态选择——torch 自己坏了不冤枉 `_C`。
487	- 归因成立的前提是事实为真：check_wheel.py 在发布前反解文件名标签、核对 `Requires-Dist` 与 `_build_meta`，保证矩阵声称的每一行与实际发的 wheel 一致——错误检查比没有检查更危险。
488	
489	## 7. 下一步学习建议
490	
491	下一讲 u9-l1 进入测试体系：四层测试如何分工，以及 `test_wheel_matrix.py` 所在的「host-only 无 GPU 测试层」能为 CI 证明什么、不能证明什么——本讲的矩阵一致性检查正是那一层的一员。继续阅读建议：先精读 [tools/make_index.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/tools/make_index.py) 的完整 docstring（索引三命名的设计论证比本讲引用的两段更细），再对照 [docs/install.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/install.md) 的 "When the import fails" 一节做一次本讲 4.4 的实践，最后带着「发布面如何被验证」的问题进入 u9 单元。

# wheel 矩阵与 ABI 匹配

## 1. 本讲目标

u8-l2 讲了「一个 wheel 是怎么被正确构建出来的」，u1-l3 讲了「作为用户应该敲哪条命令」。本讲补上中间那一层工程：一次 release 发布的 36 个 wheel 如何被组织成一张机器可读的矩阵、为什么裸 `pip install fast-ulysses` 会在**任何** torch 上都「成功」却装错行、`fast-ulysses wheel-url` 如何替你在四根轴上挑行，以及当扩展加载失败时 `_diagnose` 如何把动态链接器的原始报错翻译成「哪根轴错了」。学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 复述 [wheel_matrix.json](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/wheel_matrix.json) 的行结构，并推导「36 个 wheel」这个数字。
2. 解释 PEP 440 local version 的排序规则如何让 `pip install fast-ulysses` 解析到最高标签、进而静默把你的 torch 换成 2.13。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲不需要 GPU，但需要几块拼图：

- **PEP 440 版本号与 local version**：`0.2.0+torch210cu128` 中 `+` 之后的部分叫**局部版本（local version / 本地标签）**。两条规则是本讲的火药引线：(a) 局部版本参与排序——同一公开版本下，带标签的高于不带的，标签之间逐段比较；(b) **如果版本说明符（specifier）自己不带标签，比较时完全忽略候选的标签**——`==0.2.0` 因此同时匹配 `0.2.0` 和全部 8 个 `0.2.0+torch…`。
- **ABI（应用二进制接口）与 name mangling**：u8-l2 讲过 `_C.so` 里嵌着 `c10d::Work` 虚表、pybind11 模块和 `TORCH_LIBRARY` 注册，C++ 编译器把这些签名编码成 `_ZN3c10…` 这样的符号名。torch 换 minor 时这些 mangled 名字会变，于是旧 `.so` 里的引用变成**悬空的 `undefined symbol`**。
- **动态链接词汇**：加载 `.so` 时，动态链接器 `ld.so` 按 `DT_NEEDED` 条目（soname，如 `libcudart.so.12`）找依赖库；找不到 soname 报 `cannot open shared object file`，符号缺失报 `undefined symbol`。这两种报错**都不说**是 torch 轴还是 CUDA 轴错了——这正是 `_diagnose` 存在的理由。
- **wheel 文件名的 tag**：`fast_ulysses-0.2.0+torch210cu128-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl` 中，`+torch210cu128` 是版本的一部分（PEP 440 local version），`cp312` 是解释器 tag，`manylinux_2_28_x86_64` 是平台 tag。
- **`_build_meta.py`**：u8-l2 讲过 setup.py 在构建时把它写在扩展旁边，记录 `TORCH_ABI`、`CUDA_VERSION`、`WHEEL_TAG` 等事实——本讲里它是 `_diagnose` 的「built 侧」数据源。
- 承接 u1-l3：wheel 专用索引、`--no-build-isolation`、`doctor` 的用法已讲过，本讲钻进它们的**实现与论证**。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 wheel_matrix 行结构：8 行 × 4 个 Python + 4 个无标签行 = 36

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

一次 release 的发布面不是「一个 wheel」，而是一张 **(torch minor × CUDA major)** 的矩阵。为什么恰好是这两根轴？因为 `.so` 链接的东西决定了它能在哪运行：torch **minor** 必须精确匹配（嵌着 `c10d::Work` 虚表、pybind11 模块和 `TORCH_LIBRARY` 注册，都活不过一次 minor 升级），CUDA 只需 **major** 匹配（扩展从 toolkit 只链 `libcudart.so.<major>`，别的什么都不链——u8-l2 与 check_wheel 都断言过这一点）。

`wheel_matrix.json` 就是这张矩阵的机器可读快照，`wheel-url` 子命令读它、`test_wheel_matrix.py` 校验它。它的行还有一个特殊标记：PyPI 拒收带 local version 的包，所以**恰好一行**去掉标签上 PyPI，用 `"pypi": true` 标出。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

一个 release 的 wheel 总数：

\[ 36 = \underbrace{8_{\text{行}} \times 4_{\text{cp310--cp313}}}_{\text{带标签，走索引/find-links}} + \underbrace{4_{\text{cp}}}_{\text{无标签，上 PyPI}} \]

每行的 local version 标签由 `_tag` 推导：

\[ \texttt{tag}(r) = \texttt{torch}\{M\}\{m\}\,\texttt{cu}\{C\text{ 去掉点}\} \]

例如 `torch=2.10.0, cuda=12.8` → `torch210cu128`。注意两个「只取一部分」：

- 行里的 `torch` 字段写着完整版本（`"2.10.0"`），但匹配与标签只用 `major.minor`；
- `cuda` 字段写着 `12.8`/`12.9`/`13.0`，但匹配只用 major。

行的**顺序**也有语义：`_match` 成功时用 `next(...)` 取第一个满足条件的行，而 PyPI 行被刻意放在最后一行——它同时是排序最高的标签（见 4.2）。

**练习 3**：为什么 PyPI 行只能有一行，且必须去掉 local version？
**答案**：PyPI 拒收带 PEP 440 local version 的上传（见 docs/install.md L120-121），所以恰好一行以无标签形式上 PyPI；它的元数据是 `Requires-Dist: torch==2.13.*`。多于一行会同名同版本冲突，零行则裸 `pip install` 完全找不到包——一行是这个约束下唯一的解，代价见 4.2。

### 4.2 PEP 440 局部版本陷阱：裸 pip install 为什么会静默换 torch

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

三条 PEP 440 规则合谋出一个陷阱：

1. **局部版本参与排序**：\( v < v{+}\ell \)（同公开版本下带标签的高于不带的），标签之间**逐段**比较（数值段按数、字母段按字典序）。
2. **不带标签的 specifier 忽略候选的标签**：`==0.2.0` 匹配 `0.2.0` 和所有 `0.2.0+…`。
3. **pip 在多个匹配中取最高版本**。

于是对任何容纳了多于一行 wheel 的文件集（`--find-links`、`--extra-index-url`、一个装满 wheel 的目录、乃至 PyPI 本身），不带标签的请求都解析到**排序最高的那个标签**——与本机 torch 是什么完全无关。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

一次 release 的 9 个版本工件（8 带标签 + 1 无标签）的排序链：

\[ \texttt{0.2.0} < \texttt{0.2.0+torch210cu128} < \texttt{0.2.0+torch210cu130} < \texttt{0.2.0+torch211cu128} < \cdots < \texttt{0.2.0+torch213cu130} \]

specifier 语义形式化：

\[ v \in \mathrm{match}(\texttt{==0.2.0}) \iff v_{\text{public}} = \texttt{0.2.0} \quad (\text{标签被忽略}) \]

由此，「裸 `pip install fast-ulysses`」的完整事故链是：

```text
pip install fast-ulysses
  └─ PyPI 只有 torch213cu130（无标签形式），无需选择
     └─ 其元数据 Requires-Dist: torch==2.13.*
        └─ 本机 torch 2.11 不满足 → pip 不会失败，
           而是从 PyPI 装 torch 2.13（不同的 torch、不同的 CUDA 构建）
              └─ 报告为「普通的依赖解析」→ 无任何警告
```

两条续发症：装完后再把 torch 重装回 2.11，就得到 4.4 的 `undefined symbol`；而之后任何 `pip install fast-ulysses` 都打印 `Requirement already satisfied`，**错误的行原地不动**（`--upgrade` 也只会升到最高标签）。唯一的根治是把标签写全：`fast-ulysses==0.2.0+torch210cu128`。

[python/fast_ulysses/cli.py:L232-L240](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/cli.py#L232-L240) —— 打印命令之后固定附上：最高标签是 `<version>+<PyPI 行标签>`，所以裸 pip 与 `==<version>` 都解析到 torch `<PyPI 行 ABI>` 的 wheel，它会「把本机的 torch 也搬到 `<PyPI 行 ABI>`。Nothing warns.」

### 4.3 wheel-url 匹配顺序：machine → python → torch minor → CUDA major

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`wheel-url` 回答「当前环境该装哪个 wheel」。四根轴的**检查顺序不是随意的**：`_match` 的 docstring 说得很清楚——按「各轴被谁决定」排序：machine 与 python 是 **wheel 自身的 tag**（auditwheel/setuptools 决定，装完就不可变），先查；torch minor 与 CUDA major 是 **`.so` 钉住的轴**，需要现场读 torch 才能查。

两个容易忽略的精度选择：

- **CUDA 只比 major**：扩展从 toolkit 只链 `libcudart.so.<major>`，check_wheel.py 断言的也恰是这么多——所以 `12.8` 与 `12.9` 的环境装同一个 `cu128`/`cu129` 行（按各自 major）。
- **torch minor 按整数比较**：`_abi` 把 `"2.9"` 转成 `(2, 9)`、`"2.10"` 转成 `(2, 10)`。字符串排序会给出 `"2.9" > "2.10"` 的假象——这与 PEP 440 对公开版本的数值语义是同一个陷阱。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

`_match` 的完整判定序（伪代码）：

```text
_match(matrix, live, machine):
  1 machine  ≠ matrix.machine      → "no wheel for {machine}…"           + 源码构建
  2 python   ∉ matrix.pythons      → "no wheel for {python}…"            + 换解释器/源码构建
  3 torch 不可导入（"unimportable"）→ "torch does not import here…"       + 先装 torch
  4 torch_abi ∉ 发布的 minor 集合   → "no wheel for torch {abi}…"
        │  附「.so 嵌 c10d::Work 虚表/pybind11/TORCH_LIBRARY」的解释
        └ 选项：pip install "torch=={最近的发布 minor}.*" 再跑一次，或源码构建
  5 same = 同 minor 的行; majors = 它们的 CUDA major 集合
    live.cuda ∈ {None, unknown}    → CPU/ROCm torch，每个 wheel 都链 libcudart
    live.cuda.major ∉ majors       → "no wheel for CUDA {cuda}…
                                      A CUDA major mismatch fails at import on
                                      libcudart, and no LD_LIBRARY_PATH fixes it."
  6 返回 same 中 CUDA major 相同的那一行（next(...)）
```

第 4 步的「最近建议」逻辑：live 的 minor 低于最低发布值时建议最低那档，否则（高于最高档）建议最高那档。

### 4.4 导入失败归因：_diagnose 的四分类

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

`.so` 加载失败时，`ld.so` 只会说两种话：`undefined symbol: _ZN3c10…`（某个 mangled 符号找不到）或 `libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file`（某个 soname 找不到）。**两种话都不说本项目的两根钉子轴——torch minor、CUDA major——哪根错了**。`_diagnose` 的职责就是补上这个命名：拿两份数据做对照——

- **built 侧**：`_build_meta.py` 里 setup.py 烘进去的构建事实（`TORCH_ABI`、`CUDA_VERSION` 等）；
- **live 侧**：当前环境的 `torch.__version__`、`torch.version.cuda`、解释器 tag。

它只在失败路径上被导入（「working load pays nothing for it」）。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

`_verdict` 的分支表（按代码顺序）：

| # | 条件 | 归因 | 修复指向 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | live torch 本身导不了 | 「loader 报错是 torch 自己的」 | 先修/装 torch |
| 2 | built 为空（`_build_meta.py` 缺失） | 「unknown build，无从对照」 | 重新构建或换正规 wheel |
| 3 | 报错含 `undefined symbol` 且 minor 失配 | **torch minor ABI 不匹配** | 装与本 torch 配套的构建 |
| 4 | 报错含 `undefined symbol` 且 minor 一致 | 「缺的符号不是 torch minor 引起的」 | 另找原因 |
| 5 | 报错含 `libcudart` 且 major 失配 | **CUDA major 不匹配** | 装对应 CUDA major 的行 |
| 6 | 报错含 `libcudart` 且 major 一致 | 「cudart 装了但没有地方找得到它」 | 查 torch/nvidia wheel 安装 |
| 7 | 以上皆不中 | 「loader 消息本身就是全部」 | 兜底 |

一个容易忽略的细节：`explain` 报告的**主语**是动态选择的——torch 导不了时报 `torch failed to load`，否则报 `fast_ulysses._C failed to load`。因为 `__init__.py` 里 `import torch` 先于 `import ._C`，把 torch 的失败错怪到 `_C` 头上会把读者引向错误的排查方向。

归因的**前提是 built 侧事实为真**——这正是发布管线里 check_wheel.py 的工作（4.4.3 末条）。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
